//: The ledger model needs no composite indexes. Every query it makes is single-field, and Firestore indexes those automatically: `ledgers` by array-contains on memberIds, `entries` by date within one ledger, `templates` by name within one ledger. Keeping a ledger's documents underneath it, rather than in top-level collections filtered by ledgerId, is what removes the need for composite indexes — the same shape that makes the queries authorizable at all.
//_removed: A composite index on expenses (groupId ascending, createdAt descending) served the old group expense list. Nothing queries expenses that way now: the migration filters by groupId alone and sorts in memory, deliberately, so a migration is never the thing that discovers a missing index.
